nodes.label: RAG Answer Token Cost
nodes.rationale: Averaged over 10 topically matched queries: ~417 prompt + ~343 completion = ~760 tokens per LLM answer. Reported in tokens rather than euros/dollars because the monetary cost depends on the chosen provider's pricing, while the token count is provider-independent and converts directly.

nodes.label: Data-Sovereignty Deployment Mode
nodes.rationale: For GDPR/regulated scenarios where data must never leave controlled infrastructure, `docker compose --profile local-llm up` runs a local llama.cpp server so the RAG step makes no external call. The app is provider-agnostic: the same LLM_BASE_URL swap works with Ollama, vLLM or TGI.

nodes.label: Dataset Selection (demo / nfcorpus)
nodes.rationale: The 10 sample docs are self-referentially about search/RAG, which demos cleanly but proves nothing about scale. NFCorpus is indexed into a separate suffixed index so both corpora stay searchable side by side with no restart or env var.

nodes.label: Search Exposed as an MCP Tool
nodes.rationale: Offered as an addition alongside the REST API, not a replacement; exposes one `search` tool wrapping the same answer_search() logic the REST endpoint uses.
nodes.norm_label: search exposed as an mcp tool

nodes.label: Agentic Search Mode
nodes.rationale: Opt-in via "agentic": true. Useful for vague queries needing a refined follow-up search. use_llm_answer does not apply — the agentic loop always uses the LLM both to decide and to answer.

nodes.label: Hybrid Search API (README, German)
nodes.rationale: German-language mirror of the English README, kept in sync section for section; the project targets German-market roles, so the bilingual pair is itself a portfolio signal.

nodes.label: Ubiquitous Language Glossary
nodes.rationale: Deliberately lean — a term is added only once actually resolved, filled in lazily by the domain-modeling skill. An empty glossary is considered fine for a fresh project.

nodes.label: Search Answering (deep module)
nodes.rationale: Owns the /search request end to end and stays framework-agnostic: raises the LLM SDK's own exceptions rather than HTTPException, leaving HTTP translation to the route. Named 'Search Answering', not 'search orchestration' or 'search service' — there is one function, not a service layer.

nodes.label: elasticsearch Compose Service
nodes.rationale: Single-node with xpack.security disabled and a 512m heap — demo-scale defaults, not production hardening.

nodes.label: local-llm Compose Profile
nodes.rationale: Gated behind a Compose profile so the fast default path (bring your own cloud key) stays untouched; runs llama.cpp's server with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct GGUF and an enforced --api-key.

nodes.label: CI Pipeline (lint + test)
nodes.rationale: Runs ruff check then pytest on push to main and on every pull request, pinned to Python 3.12 on ubuntu-latest.

nodes.label: /rebuild Command
nodes.rationale: Exists because the api container does not pick up code changes automatically; also checks whether index_config.py changed recently, since that requires deleting and reseeding the Elasticsearch index before search is testable.

nodes.label: /startup Command
nodes.rationale: Session-start routine: verify the graphify graph exists, confirm the agent-skills docs are current, then print the newest handoff doc for this repo. Handoffs deliberately live outside the repo and are never auto-loaded.

nodes.label: ADR-0001: Local sentence-transformers, not Ollama
nodes.rationale: Keeps embeddings in-process via all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384 dims). Ollama would add a service the demo depends on being up and warmed, with no functional payoff at this corpus size, and swapping models changes vector dimensionality — forcing an index delete and reseed. MODEL_NAME stays hardcoded as a deliberate simplicity choice; the LLM-client config seam does not generalize because embeddings.py has no equivalent SDK abstraction.

nodes.label: ADR-0002: llama-server, not Ollama, for local LLM mode
nodes.rationale: Ollama does not enforce API-key auth by default, so the AuthenticationError branch this project showcases would be silently dead code against it. llama-server genuinely 401s on a wrong key and is CPU-first/GGUF, fitting 'runs on a laptop'. vLLM is the most spec-faithful but assumes a GPU; TGI's compat layer is least mature; LocalAI is redundant with Ollama. Mirror image of ADR-0001: there is no in-process equivalent for chat generation, so the question is which server, not whether.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002: llama-server, not ollama, for local llm mode

nodes.label: ADR Index and Authoring Rules
nodes.rationale: Write an ADR when a decision is hard to reverse, spans services, had a serious alternative, or will prompt a 'why did we do it this way' in six months. Never overwrite one — mark it Superseded and write a new one, because the old reasoning is the context the new decision makes sense in.

nodes.label: Domain Docs Reading Protocol
nodes.rationale: Single-context layout: CONTEXT.md plus docs/adr/ at the root. Missing files are passed over silently rather than flagged, because the domain-modeling skill creates them lazily once terms actually get resolved.

nodes.label: GitHub Issue Tracker Conventions
nodes.rationale: Issues and specs live as GitHub issues driven through the gh CLI. PRs are explicitly not treated as a request surface for this repo. Wayfinding uses one map issue with native GitHub issue dependencies for blocking.

nodes.label: Agentic RAG Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Eight sequenced tasks from adding anyio through live end-to-end verification, each with its own verification step.
nodes.community_name: Agentic RAG via in-process MCP dogfooding

nodes.label: Agentic RAG via In-Process MCP Dogfooding
nodes.rationale: Additive by design: agentic defaults to False so the fixed pipeline is byte-identical to before. Explicitly not a general-purpose agent framework — one tool, one bounded loop, no planning or memory beyond a single request.
nodes.community_name: Agentic RAG via in-process MCP dogfooding
nodes.norm_label: agentic rag via in-process mcp dogfooding

nodes.label: In-Memory MCP Transport
nodes.rationale: Uses create_client_server_memory_streams rather than stdio/subprocess: an anyio task group runs the existing MCP server against one end while a ClientSession talks to the other, in-process. Avoids a subprocess spawn and reloading the embedding model per request — a protocol-shaped call, not a process boundary.

nodes.label: Three-Round Tool-Calling Loop
nodes.rationale: Capped at 3 rounds; after the cap the tools argument is dropped to force a text-only response. Marked in-code as a ponytail shortcut — fixed cap, made configurable only if real usage needs deeper loops.
nodes.community_name: Agentic RAG via in-process MCP dogfooding

nodes.label: Live MCP Tool-Schema Discovery
nodes.rationale: session.list_tools() returns the real search tool schema, converted to OpenAI tool-calling format. Discovered from the live server rather than hand-duplicated, so a parameter change is picked up automatically.
nodes.community_name: Agentic RAG via in-process MCP dogfooding

nodes.label: Built-in Search UI
nodes.rationale: Single self-contained HTML page served at / — no build step, no framework, no external assets, so the demo needs nothing beyond the running container.

nodes.label: Dataset Toggle Control
nodes.rationale: Two buttons above the query box; switching datasets also swaps the description line and the example query, so the user sees what each corpus contains instead of guessing.

nodes.label: Search UI Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Centred single-column layout on a pale blue gradient. Top to bottom: title and tagline, a card holding the Demo/NFCorpus dataset toggle with its description line, the query input, a 'Generate answer' checkbox with the EN/DE toggle, and a right-aligned Search button. Below the card, the RAG answer sits in a tinted panel labelled ANSWER, followed by white result cards each showing a document title with its RRF score and body text. Demonstrates that the answer is visually separated from the ranked hits that grounded it.

nodes.label: Search UI Demo Recording
nodes.rationale: Animated walkthrough of the same UI: a search on the Demo corpus resolving from a 'Searching…' state to an answer plus ranked hits, then a switch to NFCorpus which swaps both the description line and the example query, a second search against the medical corpus, and a scroll through the results. Shows the two corpora are live side by side with no restart.

nodes.label: graphify update reverts the curated doc layer
nodes.rationale: `graphify update .` re-extracts every file its structural extractor owns, Markdown included, and drops all nodes carrying that source_file first. Hand-curated concept nodes are replaced by heading-level nodes under different IDs, taking ~38 cross-file rationale_for/references edges and the 21 curated community names with them (308->307 nodes, 604->577 edges). Not idempotent: every run, not only on change. Backs the curated graph up to graphify-out/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ first.
